fig02_satellite_bands.png: Figure 2. Sentinel-2 bands (B3, B4, B8, B11), a NIR-Red-Green false-colour composite and the cloud/shadow mask for the 2025 composite. Grey stretches use the 2nd-98th percentile.
fig06_landcover_distribution.png: Figure 6. Reference land-cover composition (ESA WorldCover codes), and how the high-LST risk class and mean LST differ among classes. The dashed line marks the expected 25% if risk were independent of land cover.
fig03_ndvi_distribution_map.png: Figure 3. NDVI maps for 2019 and 2025 (cloud-masked composites) and the corresponding value distributions.
fig04_ndwi_mndwi_maps.png: Figure 4. NDWI and MNDWI for 2025 and agreement of the water masks (index > 0). 'NDWI only' pixels are candidate false water detections (for example built-up land) and require inspection against reference data.
fig05_multitemporal_change_map.png: Figure 5. Rule-based candidate change from index differences (2019 to 2025). These are spectral-index changes, not validated land-cover transitions: phenology (crop harvest timing), residual cloud and soil moisture can all produce index changes without a land-cover change.
fig07_correlation_heatmap.png: Figure 7. Spearman rank correlation among sampled predictors and LST. LST is shown for exploration only and is not a model input. Strongly correlated predictors (for example NDVI and its neighbourhood mean) share explanatory credit.
fig01_study_area_map.png: Figure 1. Study area (Natore District, Bangladesh; CRS EPSG:32645). (a) Elevation. (b) 303 spatial blocks split into training, buffer and one contiguous held-out test region, with a subset of sampled pixels.
fig09_roc_comparison.png: Figure 9. ROC curves for the four classifiers evaluated on the held-out contiguous test region.
fig10_confusion_matrices.png: Figure 10. Confusion matrices on the held-out region (counts; percentages are row-normalised recall per observed class).
fig13_model_performance_comparison.png: Figure 13. Model comparison. (a) Five metrics on the held-out region. (b) ROC-AUC under buffered spatial cross-validation (training region) against the held-out test region.
fig08_feature_importance.png: Figure 8. Feature importance for XGBoost: (a) model-agnostic permutation importance on the held-out region (mean ± SD over repeats); (b) mean absolute SHAP value. Agreement between the two supports the ranking.
fig11_shap_summary_beeswarm.png: Figure 11. SHAP beeswarm summary for XGBoost. Each point is a held-out pixel; colour shows the feature value. SHAP describes the fitted model's behaviour, not a causal effect.
fig11b_shap_feature_importance.png: Figure 11b. Global SHAP importance (mean absolute SHAP value) for XGBoost.
fig12_shap_dependence.png: Figure 12. SHAP dependence plots for the two most influential features of XGBoost; colour shows the feature with the strongest estimated interaction.

fig15_rag_retrieval_similarity.png: Figure 15. Best query-to-document cosine similarity for a hand-written evaluation question set. Red boxes mark the document that should answer the question. Out-of-scope questions (no red box) should stay below the evidence threshold.
